turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi doctor—I'm a 31-year-old woman. For the past five months I've had intermittent flank pain, and I’ve had five urinary tract infections over the last two years. I’m not having any recent fever, nausea, or vomiting, and my urinary habits are mostly normal except during those UTIs.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any change in the shape or contour of either breast—such as one becoming noticeably different in size, shape, or position compared with before? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any changes in breast size, shape, or position.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **Have you had any abdominal (belly) pain recently?**
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t had any abdominal (belly) pain recently; it’s mainly the intermittent flank pain that’s been going on.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or run-down more than usual lately (for example, less energy for everyday activities)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t felt particularly weak or run-down; my energy for everyday activities has been pretty normal. The main issue has been the intermittent flank pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had diarrhea recently—meaning loose or watery stools more than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t had diarrhea or any significant change in my bowel movements; everything has been normal except when I’m dealing with a UTI.”

turns.doctor_question: Are you having **profuse sweating**—for example, sweating so much that your clothes or bedding become noticeably wet, even when you’re not doing heavy physical activity?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t had profuse sweating like that. I’m not noticing sweating that soaks my clothes or bedding, and my symptoms have mainly been intermittent flank pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have pain in your wrist (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I don’t have pain in my wrist.”

turns.doctor_question: When you wake up in the morning, do you have stiffness in your joints or muscles that lasts **more than 30 minutes** before it starts to ease? (Yes or no.)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—when I wake up I don’t have joint or muscle stiffness that lasts more than 30 minutes; it generally eases quickly.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a breast lump or mass that feels **fixed in place**—meaning it doesn’t move much when you gently press it? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any breast lump or any fixed-in-place mass.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you currently have any pain in your knee (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I don’t currently have pain in my knee.”

turns.doctor_question: When you walk, do you get pain or cramping in your calf that improves or goes away when you stop and rest? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I don’t get pain or cramping in my calf when I walk that improves with rest; it hasn’t been happening.”
